- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.00) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is >+2% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias and reduce by 0.5–1.5% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-1.00” entries, model underperforms; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to compensate for bearish sentiment lag.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility >0.3.
